title: Numerical semiampleness of nef adjoint classes on compact Kähler manifolds
main_claim: Let X be a compact Kähler manifold with a klt SNC boundary B. Suppose K_X+B is pseudo-effective, M is a nef rational line bundle, and D=K_X+B+M is nef. Then D has the same real Chern class as some semiample rational line bundle. The proof goes through a stronger result (Thm 1.2). After a modification, mu^*(J+M) ≡ P+R, where P is semiample and R=N(mu^*(J+M)) is the negative part. In addition, a(T)=0 forces c_1(M)=0. Both statements are proved together by induction on dimension.

issues.location: Sec 2 (Thm 2.2 / Prop 2.3 / Prop 2.4) and Sec 5 Lemma zero:geometric-reduction
issues.description: The result depends on very large external inputs, so it is conditional rather than unconditional. These inputs are: ordinary Kähler log abundance in every dimension, in divisorial form (companion K, Thm 2.13 and Prop 3.8, with the Iitaka hypothesis supplied by LI Cor 6.2); the projective positive-part theorem (companion P, Prop 8.1), together with termination of a generalized klt MMP for pseudo-effective generalized pairs (P, Thm 2.3); and the MWWZ Kähler BBY decomposition (Cor 1.4), applied to a klt pair whose boundary may be nonzero. I found no circularity within this paper, but the companions were not audited here.
issues.evidence: Prop pre:projective's proof runs 'a terminating generalized klt program as in [P, Thm 2.3]'. For non-big pseudo-effective boundaries this is open in the literature. Thm pre:ordinary is ordinary abundance in arbitrary dimension, cited from K.

coverage: I read every section and checked the following in detail. Sec 3: the descent of the current over the smooth locus; the Zariski-lemma matrix C (Ca=0, Cx≥0, kernel = R·a when the graph is connected); the use of equidimensionality and negativity to kill D_0; the rationality of the descended class; and meridian-order descent of flat lines. Sec 4: the ramification index e and root order e-1-p of the cyclic cover; the vector-field lifting step via a split extension; the descent of the invariant field, where exponents are ≡0 or ≡1 mod e against a pole bound of e-2; the period-rank equality giving P big; effectivity of D_Z; and klt crepant pushdown. Sec 5: the tangent-line bound in the point-pole lemma; the normalization r→∞; the K-intersection constants (n+1)/2^n·qv and d·C(2n,n)/4^n·qv^2; the M_u restriction and vol(M)~q; Seshadri ≥ c·q^{1/d}; the GRR formula for B_0 and the Khovanskii–Teissier log-concavity bound; slope descent; the final slice cancellation to 2a^*P+(s+2q)a^*L-c·s·F ≥ 0 and the resulting contradiction; and the final ± pseudo-effectivity argument for N_0. I also checked the geometric reduction (product/fiber intersection, the one-form produced by moving correspondences). Sec 6: the countable twists are fixed before the fiber is chosen; the section-lifting/algebraic-reduction contradiction; the incidence-cycle constancy argument; and the Λ|_G triviality check, where R_F cancels. Sec 7: the codim-2 Hodge-index lemma; the HX length estimate with b>2n, which keeps the program over W; the Stein factorization giving dim Z = a(T); and the bookkeeping of negative parts. The middle Sec 5 lemmas (incidence pole b_V ≥ s-C, monomial-count determinant order) were only skimmed. The earlier sibling pass reports checking them.
